title: HEART score
subtitle: Acute coronary syndrome in adults with chest pain
question: In an adult with chest pain in the emergency department, how likely is acute coronary syndrome (ACS)?

options.label: ST depression or transient ST elevation

inputs.label: Risk factors
inputs.note: Risk factors: currently treated diabetes, current or recent (less than 1 month) smoker, diagnosed hypertension, diagnosed hyperlipidemia, family history of CAD, and obesity.

options.label: 3 or more risk factors, or known CAD
1 to 3 times the upper limit of normal
More than 3 times the upper limit of normal

pretest.source: the overall rate of ACS in the validation studies

evidence.validation: Quality score 1 (scale 1 to 4): test set from a distinct population.
evidence.comment: Likelihood ratios ranged from 0.20 for low risk to 13 for very high risk; the likelihood of ACS ranged from 2.9% to 66%.

references.citation: Fanaroff AC, Rymer JA, Goldstein SA, et al. Does this patient with chest pain have acute coronary syndrome? The Rational Clinical Examination systematic review. JAMA. 2015;314(18):1955-1965.
